_comment: IR agent Datadog monitors, applied by Apply-DatadogConfig.ps1.
API: https://docs.datadoghq.com/api/latest/monitors/
create POST /api/v1/monitor
read   GET  /api/v1/monitor/{monitor_id}
list   GET  /api/v1/monitor?name=<substring>
update PUT  /api/v1/monitor/{monitor_id}
Required create fields per the v1 OpenAPI spec (schema Monitor): type and
query. name, message, tags and options are optional but all set here.
IDENTITY. Monitor names are NOT unique in this org -- dev and test both
carry a monitor called 'IR Agent - Error rate climbing' and so on. Verified
live 2026-08-26 via GET /api/v1/monitor: the dev copies are 21577973-
21577978 (ml_app:ir-agent, env:dev) and the test copies are 21633848-
21633852 (ml_app:ir-agent, env:test). The _datadog_id below pins
each entry to its TEST monitor. The apply script matches on that id first
and falls back to an exact name+query match; an ambiguous fallback is a
refusal, never a guess.
PLACEHOLDER THRESHOLDS. Four of the five monitors below carry a message
beginning 'PLACEHOLDER THRESHOLD -- ...'. None of those numeric thresholds
are tuned from real incident data; they exist so the monitors are wired now
and get real numbers later. No @-notification handles are set -- routing is
a separate decision. Do NOT invent replacement thresholds here.
ASCII NOTE. The live monitors carry an em-dash after 'PLACEHOLDER
THRESHOLD'. These JSON files are ASCII-only (non-ASCII punctuation parses
as ANSI under Windows PowerShell 5.1 and breaks string terminators), so the
em-dash is written as '--'. Applying this file therefore rewrites the
message text on the five live monitors -- the only content change from the
Terraform originals.
COST MONITOR UNITS. ml_obs.span.llm.total.cost is NANODOLLARS. The
TYPE NORMALIZATION. Datadog stores some 'metric alert' submissions as
'query alert' and reports the stored type back -- verified live 2026-08-26
on 21633848 and 21633850, which Terraform declared as 'metric alert' and
the API returns as 'query alert'. They are the same monitor. The apply
script treats live 'query alert' as satisfying a desired 'metric alert' so
this does not read as drift on every run.
OPTIONS ARE COMPARED AS A SUBSET. Datadog adds its own defaults
(include_tags, new_host_delay, notify_audit, require_full_window, silenced).
The apply script checks only that the options declared here are present with
these values; it does not try to strip Datadog's defaults. A PUT carrying
only these keys leaves the rest at their defaults.

monitors.name: IR Agent - Error rate climbing
monitors.message: PLACEHOLDER THRESHOLD -- set before the September correctness criteria land; revisit. IR agent span error rate has climbed above the placeholder threshold over the last hour.

monitors.name: IR Agent - p95 latency regression
monitors.message: PLACEHOLDER THRESHOLD -- set before the September correctness criteria land; revisit. IR agent trace p95 duration has exceeded the placeholder threshold over the last hour.

monitors._note: Nanodollars. 5,000,000,000 ns = $5.00/day. The figure is a deliberately round, generous placeholder chosen to avoid false positives while the agent has no stable daily spend baseline -- NOT a computed multiple of any observed figure.
monitors.name: IR Agent - Daily spend breach
monitors.message: PLACEHOLDER THRESHOLD -- set before the September correctness criteria land; revisit. IR agent daily LLM cost has exceeded the placeholder threshold. NOTE: ml_obs.span.llm.total.cost is in NANODOLLARS -- this threshold (5,000,000,000) is $5.00/day, not $5,000,000,000/day. Divide by 1e9 when reading the triggering value.
monitors._options_note: renotify_interval is deliberately OMITTED, not set to 0. Datadog treats 0 as 'never renotify' and drops the key from the stored monitor entirely -- verified live 2026-08-26 on this monitor, whose options come back with no renotify_interval at all. Declaring 0 here would make the apply script report drift on every single run and never reach NO CHANGE.

monitors._note: The ONLY threshold here derived from measured traffic, not guessed. Observed peak hourly token usage was 2,334,088 (consistent across a 2-day and a 7-day window, queried 2026-08-03); 2,450,792 is that peak +5%. The original 500,000 placeholder fired immediately on normal traffic. Re-derive the same way once real prod volume exists rather than scaling by intuition. The message keeps the PLACEHOLDER prefix as it stands live.
monitors.name: IR Agent - Token spike
monitors.message: PLACEHOLDER THRESHOLD -- set before the September correctness criteria land; revisit. IR agent hourly token usage has exceeded 2,450,792 (observed peak 2,334,088 +5%, measured 2026-08-03). Either traffic genuinely grew or a prompt regression is inflating context -- check the per-model token widget on the IR Agent - Observability dashboard first.

monitors.name: IR Agent - Span volume dropped to zero
monitors.message: PLACEHOLDER THRESHOLD -- set before the September correctness criteria land; revisit. IR agent has emitted zero spans over the last 24 hours -- the agent may be down, undeployed, or Datadog ingestion may be broken.
monitors._options_note: renotify_interval omitted, not 0 -- see the note on ir_agent_daily_spend.

_disabled_reason: NOT APPLIED. Carried forward verbatim from the Terraform unit so the
intent is not lost. See ADO-200009.
Datadog's duplicate-monitor check compares only the top-level `query`
string. For a trace-analytics alert the environment scope lives in the
nested event_query search blocks, not in the outer formula, so this
monitor's outer query is byte-identical between dev and test even
though the two are correctly scoped to different environments. The API
therefore rejects the test copy as a duplicate of the dev one
(monitor 21577978, which exists and is in No Data -- verified live
2026-08-26), with 'Duplicate of an existing monitor_id'.
Under Terragrunt this single monitor blocked every downstream GCP
module in the environment, which is why it was dropped. Under the
apply script the blast radius is smaller, but the API rejection is
unchanged, so it stays out.
SECOND, INDEPENDENT BLOCKER (verified live 2026-08-26): the underlying
data does not exist. ml_obs.evaluation returns ZERO series org-wide and
the APM spans index carries no @evaluation.* facet, so even if the
duplicate check passed this monitor would evaluate 0/0 forever. Both
problems must be solved before re-enabling: emit the evaluations as a
custom metric, and give the outer query an env-distinguishing term.
The live Datadog API caps a trace-analytics alert's evaluation window
at 48h -- last('7d') and last('168h') are both rejected ('unit d must
have value between 1 and 2' / 'unit h must have value between 1 and
48'), confirmed empirically via terragrunt plan. Hence last('48h').
disabled_monitors.name: IR Agent - Evaluation pass rate
disabled_monitors.message: PLACEHOLDER THRESHOLD -- set before the September correctness criteria land; revisit. IR agent's ir_investigation_reliable evaluation pass rate has dropped below the placeholder threshold over a 48-hour window (the API caps this monitor type's evaluation window at 48h; evaluation results are span attributes, not ml_obs.* metrics, so this is a query monitor, not a metric monitor).
